items.title: Lillian De Pass Interview, 1960-06-20
items.q: My brother-in-law used to kid and say, Lynn, they ain't got no, God ain't in no lottery.

ctx.x: Oh, so you used to be pretty lucky with lottery. You used to win a lot of the time. Yes, indeed. When I was at Penn, they used to sell vengeance pebbles.

All them days was common. You'd say that was good days. You used a lottery vendor. There wasn't as much going on like you had. You had so much going on now. Look, they had lottery. How many times when my husband's eyes got bad? And he was working, but not as much, you know. And it was time of depression. Well, like when my children would need something, I'd just get out there. My brother-in-law used to kid and say, Lynn, they ain't got no, God ain't in no lottery. I said, well, he sure answers my prayer. And I'd…
Wait a minute, it's about to run off again, you know. All right.
